steps.body: On a number line, **the number farther right is always greater.** That rule still holds with negatives — which flips some intuition. −2 is greater than −5, because −2 sits to the RIGHT of −5. With negatives, the digit that LOOKS bigger (5) belongs to the SMALLER number.

widget.ltFeedback: -5 has the bigger DIGIT, but it sits farther LEFT — deeper into the negatives — so it's actually smaller. -2 is greater.
widget.eqFeedback: They're different points on the line: -2 is right of -5, so -2 is greater.
widget.successFeedback: Right — -2 is farther right on the line (closer to zero), so it's greater than -5.

hints: -2 is closer to zero, so it's greater.
explanationVariants: -2 is right of -5, so -2 is greater.
Closer to zero on the negative side means greater.

predict.prompt: On the number line, which direction means GREATER — even for negatives?

options.label: It depends which digit is bigger

predict.reveal: Greater means farther right, with no exceptions — the rule doesn't flip below zero. Digit size misleads exactly there, where −2 outranks −5.

explanationVariants: -8 is farther below zero than -3, so -8 is the colder (smaller) temperature.
-8 sits left of -3 on the line, making it the smaller value.

widget.prompt: Two mornings: -3 degrees and -8 degrees. Which temperature is COLDER (the smaller number)?
widget.ltFeedback: -3 is actually WARMER — it's closer to zero. The colder, smaller value is -8.
widget.eqFeedback: -3 and -8 are different: -8 is 5 degrees colder. The smaller (colder) one is -8.
widget.successFeedback: Right — -8 is farther below zero (left on the line), so it's colder and smaller.

steps.body: The symbols still work left-to-right on the line: **< means "left of," > means "right of."** So −5 < −2 (−5 is left of −2), and −2 > −5. A quick test: any negative number is always LESS than any positive number, and less than zero.

explanationVariants: -6 < -1 is true: -6 sits left of -1 on the line.
-6 is deeper into the negatives than -1, so -6 is the smaller one.

widget.eqFeedback: -6 and -1 aren't the same point: -1 sits five steps closer to zero, so -1 is greater. The true statement is -6 < -1.
widget.gtFeedback: This says -6 is greater, but -6 sits farther LEFT (deeper negative), so it's smaller. The true statement is -6 < -1.
widget.successFeedback: Right — -6 is left of -1 on the line, so -6 is less than -1.

predict.prompt: 0, -5, -1, -8 from smallest to largest. Where does -8 go?

options.label: First — it is the smallest, even though 8 is the biggest digit
Last among the negatives — 8 is the largest number there
Between -5 and -1, ordered by size of the digit

predict.reveal: First. On the line, -8 sits farthest LEFT, and left means smaller. The digit 8 being large is exactly what pushes it further from zero in the negative direction — bigger digit, smaller number.

widget.prompt: Arrange these from SMALLEST to largest: 0, -5, -1, -8.

misorderFeedback.feedback: 0 isn't the smallest — every negative is less than 0. The smallest here is -8, the deepest negative.

widget.missFeedback: Smallest means farthest LEFT on the line: -8, then -5, then -1, then 0. The bigger the digit on a negative, the smaller the number.
widget.successFeedback: Ordered — deepest negative first, zero last. Bigger negative digit means smaller value.

explanationVariants: Any negative is less than any positive, so -100 < 1.
-100 is left of zero and 1 is right of zero — the negative is smaller.

widget.eqFeedback: They sit on opposite sides of zero: 1 is positive, -100 is negative. 1 is greater.
widget.gtFeedback: -100 has huge digits, but it's still on the negative side of zero — smaller than any positive. 1 is greater.
widget.successFeedback: Right — any positive number beats any negative number, no matter how big the negative's digits look. 1 > -100.

hints: Which side of zero is each on?
Place all four on the line first.
Negatives go left of zero, positives right.
From smallest (farthest left): -7, then -2, then 3, then 6.
explanationVariants: Smallest to largest: -7, -2, 3, 6 — negatives first (deepest first), then positives.
-7 is farthest left, 6 farthest right; the rest fall in line between them.

misorderFeedback.feedback: -2 isn't smaller than -7 — -7 is deeper into the negatives, so -7 comes first.

widget.missFeedback: Farthest left is smallest: -7, then -2, then the positives 3 and 6. Deeper negatives are smaller; bigger positives are larger.
widget.successFeedback: Ordered — the two negatives (deepest first) come before the two positives.

takeaways: The number farther right on the line is always greater — even among negatives.
A bigger digit on a negative number means a SMALLER value (-8 < -3).
Every negative is less than zero and less than every positive.

concept.body: Quick rewind. **Farther right on the line = greater.** -1 is right of -4, so -1 is greater than -4, even though 4 looks like the bigger digit. On the negative side, bigger digits mean smaller numbers.

explanationVariants: -1 is right of -4 on the line, so -1 is greater.
-4 is deeper into the negatives, making it smaller.

-4 has the bigger digit but sits farther left, so it's smaller. -1 is greater.
